title: Reflection: power, cost, and when it is the wrong tool
hook: Reflection is how the runtime describes types that already exist in metadata. Using it as a mapper on every SQS message is how a worker misses its SLA and then fails Native AOT.

sections.heading: What reflection is for
sections.prose: The `System.Reflection` APIs (`Type`, `Assembly`, `MethodInfo`, `PropertyInfo`) let you inspect and, if you insist, invoke members by name. `object.GetType()` is the cheap entry. `GetCustomAttributes` materializes attribute instances lazily and a new instance per call. Dynamic invocation (`Invoke`, `Activator.CreateInstance`) boxes, skips some compile-time checks, and is orders of magnitude slower than a direct call. Legitimate uses: plugin hosts that load a known interface from a folder, diagnostic dumps, test frameworks, serializers that you did not write. Illegitimate uses in this codebase: discovering every `IRequestHandler` on each message, building Redis DTOs by walking properties in a loop, calling private setters to “fix” a domain entity.

snippets.label: Prefer a compiled map over Invoke
snippets.explanation: A dictionary of interfaces is wired at composition time. GetTypes plus Invoke on every message allocates, misses trimming, and hides missing methods until production.

sections.heading: Closed world: AOT, trim, and linking
sections.prose: Native AOT and the IL trimmer assume they can see every call. `GetMethod("Handle")` is a string; the trimmer may remove `Handle`. You then get `MissingMethodException` or a trim warning you ignored. Source generators and `[DynamicallyAccessedMembers]` exist because of this. If a worker publishes with `PublishAot`, treat reflection as a feature you must justify with roots, not a default architecture. Module 01 already warned that file-based apps default AOT on publish — this is where that warning bites. JSON source generation and regex source generation are the platform’s answer: inspect at compile time, emit typed code, run with no `Type.GetProperties` in the loop.

sections.heading: Privacy is not a suggestion
sections.prose: Reflection can call `non-public` members if the runtime permits it. That does not make it a supported API. A private constructor on a domain entity exists so invariants run; `ConstructorInfo.Invoke` is how you create an invalid invoice and then blame the model. Interview answer: “We could, we should not, and AOT may stop us.” Prefer InternalsVisibleTo for tests that need to construct awkward states, or public test-only factory methods marked `Experimental`.

interviewTakeaways: Reflection reads metadata that is already in the assembly; it is not a substitute for a composition root.
String-named members are invisible to the trimmer; Native AOT makes that a ship blocker.
Do not use reflection to bypass constructors that enforce invariants.
commonPitfalls: Caching Type but still calling GetCustomAttributes every request — those allocate new attribute instances.
Scanning all types in the entry assembly on startup in a Lambda — cold start pays for every unused controller-shaped class you accidentally compiled in.
Assuming BindingFlags.NonPublic is acceptable in production because tests used it.

jsTsCorrelations.note: `obj[handlerName]()` is normal JS. C# equivalent GetMethod/Invoke is a slow, trim-hostile escape hatch because types were supposed to be known at compile time.
JS objects are open at runtime. C# reflection is explicit, slower, and often replaced by source generators.
